planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Ballerina is a lily-flowered tulip prized for its unusually strong, sweet fragrance.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Ballerina carries slender, pointed-petaled flowers in a luminous tangerine-orange flushed with rose at the base, held on sturdy wind-resistant stems that open wide as the blooms mature in late spring. It is one of the most distinctly perfumed tulips in commerce, making it a favorite near paths, patios, and cut-flower beds where its scent can be appreciated up close. Deadhead after flowering and let foliage die back naturally to help the bulb recharge for a repeat show the following year.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; China Pink is a classic lily-flowered tulip and RHS Award of Garden Merit winner.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. China Pink bears slender, elegantly waisted flowers in a clear sugar-pink that deepens slightly as the blooms age, opening to reveal a creamy-white base and golden stamens against sturdy, erect stems that hold up well to wind and rain. Its refined silhouette and long vase life make it a long-favored choice for spring borders, cutting gardens, and mixed container displays. Deadhead spent flowers and allow the foliage to yellow and wither naturally before cleanup to build strength in the bulb for future seasons.

common_name: Gordon Reticulata Iris (Two-Tone Blue Dwarf Bulbous Iris)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in lean, gravelly, very well-drained soil in full sun; reticulata iris needs a dry summer dormancy and rots in heavy or poorly drained soil.

directions: Plant bulbs in fall in lean, gravelly, very well-drained soil in full sun, where the small bulbs can bake dry through summer dormancy. Gordon is an older, long-grown reticulata cultivar with distinctive two-tone flowers, pale sky-blue standards above deeper violet-blue falls marked with a bright yellow-and-white central blaze, opening low among grassy foliage in the earliest weeks of spring. Its small scale and jewel-like color make it well suited to rock gardens, raised troughs, and edging where it can be viewed up close. Let the foliage ripen and die back naturally after bloom and avoid summer watering, which encourages bulb rot.

common_name: George Reticulata Iris (Deep Plum-Purple Dwarf Bulbous Iris)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in lean, gravelly, very well-drained soil in full sun; reticulata iris needs a dry summer dormancy and rots in heavy or poorly drained soil.

directions: Plant bulbs in fall in lean, gravelly, very well-drained soil in full sun, giving the small bulbs the dry summer rest they require. George produces broad, velvety plum-purple petals splashed with a bold yellow-and-white blotch on the falls, among the darkest and most saturated colors in the reticulata group, blooming low to the ground in very early spring often alongside snowdrops. The compact habit and intense color read best planted in drifts near a path edge, rock garden, or container where the short bloom period can be enjoyed at close range. Allow foliage to die back naturally and withhold summer irrigation to prevent bulb rot during dormancy.

common_name: Natascha Reticulata Iris (Fragrant White-and-Blue Dwarf Bulbous Iris)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in lean, gravelly, very well-drained soil in full sun; reticulata iris needs a dry summer dormancy and rots in heavy or poorly drained soil.

directions: Plant bulbs in fall in lean, gravelly, very well-drained soil in full sun, where the small bulbs can dry out through their summer dormancy. Natascha opens nearly white, finely veined in pale blue with a bright yellow flash on the falls, and carries a notable sweet scent that is unusually strong for such a diminutive flower, blooming low among grassy foliage in the earliest weeks of spring. Its pale, luminous coloring shows especially well against dark mulch or paired with deeper blue or purple reticulata cultivars in a mixed rock garden planting. Let foliage yellow and wither naturally after bloom and avoid summer watering, which can rot the small bulbs.

common_name: Frank Elder Reticulata Iris (Pale Blue-Grey Dwarf Bulbous Iris)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in lean, gravelly, very well-drained soil in full sun; this reticulata-group hybrid needs a dry summer dormancy and rots in heavy or poorly drained soil.

directions: Plant bulbs in fall in lean, gravelly, very well-drained soil in full sun, mimicking the dry alpine summers this hybrid's parents come from. Frank Elder, a cross between Iris histrioides and Iris winogradowii, produces unusually large, rounded flowers in a soft blue-grey infused with yellow-green and lightly spotted on the falls around a yellow crest, a quieter, more muted palette than most reticulata cultivars. It received the RHS Award of Merit and remains valued for extending the color range of these earliest-blooming bulbous iris. Allow foliage to ripen and die back naturally after flowering and keep the planting dry through summer dormancy to avoid bulb rot.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society Award of Merit record
